title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages (Longue Marche continuation, ms. p. 712). X is a connected, locally connected topos with geometric point x0. Γ is a group of automorphisms of X. π = π1(X, x0), and the equivariant fundamental group fits in an extension 1→π→π1(X,Γ;x0)→Γ→1. One passes to a Γ-stable abelian quotient M of π^ab, giving an extension 1→M→M̃→Γ→1, with M written additively and Γ acting on M through it. The objects studied are abelian M-coverings, i.e. M-torsors E (affine spaces under M) on which M̃ acts compatibly: M by translations, the rest by affine maps.

On this page. The action gives a homomorphism M̃ → Aff(E) ≅ M ⋊ Aut(M). Its image M̃̃ is a quotient of M̃ in which M still injects (as translations). This gives an extension (283) 1→M→M̃̃→Γ̃̃→1, where Γ̃̃ = image of Γ in Aut(M) (the linear parts) acts faithfully on M.

This extension is split, because Aff(E) splits once an origin is chosen. The fact that it comes from the affine action (Θ_ũ) gives extra structure: a distinguished M-conjugacy class of splittings.

Precisely, there is a canonical map (285) E → Scind(M̃̃ as an extension of Γ̃̃ by M). It sends a point x to its stabiliser in M̃̃, a complement to M. The map is M-equivariant: translation on E corresponds to conjugation by inner automorphisms (by elements of M) on splittings. Its image is exactly one M-conjugacy class.

x and y have the same image iff u = y−x lies in M^Γ = M^{Γ̃̃}. Hence (286): E → Scind is injective iff M^Γ = 0, and in that case E is identified with one M-conjugacy class of splittings of M̃̃.

In modern terms: the splittings of M⋊G form a torsor under Z^1(G,M). An M-conjugacy orbit of splittings is M/M^G, via coboundaries u ↦ (g ↦ gu − u). Points of an affine G-space correspond to complements, i.e. to the stabilisers of points. The next page packages all this as a Proposition about Γ-equivariant abelian coverings. This is presumably in service of describing equivariant abelian coverings of (X, Γ), and ultimately of sections of fundamental-group extensions (e.g. the S_3-action on M_{0,3} seen on the previous page).
errors: No mathematical error. The claim that extension (283) is 'triviale' is justified only implicitly: it holds because M̃̃ sits inside Aff(E) and the stabiliser of any point of E gives a complement. Grothendieck states it without spelling this out.
There is minor notational drift: (285) writes Γ̃ where Γ̃̃ is meant, and M^Γ = M^{Γ̃} should read M^{Γ̃̃}. These are harmless because Γ acts through Γ̃̃.

ideas.what: An affine action of an extension M̃ of Γ by an abelian group M on an M-torsor E. Its image in Aff(E) = M⋊Aut(M) gives a split extension of the faithful image Γ̃̃ by M.
ideas.modern_name: affine representations / affine group M ⋊ GL(M); faithful quotient of an extension

ideas.what: Points of E map to splittings (stabilisers), equivariantly for translation versus inner conjugation. The image is one M-conjugacy class, and the fibres are M^Γ-cosets, so the map is injective iff M^Γ = 0.
ideas.modern_name: correspondence between fixed points / complements and 1-cocycles; conjugacy classes of complements ↔ H^1(G,M); stabiliser M^G of a complement

deep.surprise_reason: The page works out standard facts about affine actions and complements in split extensions (H^1/Z^1 bookkeeping), as a lemma toward equivariant abelian coverings of a topos with group action. It is correct and routine; nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'opère fidèlement sur M' (the first word, 'injectivement', is struck out and replaced by 'fidèlement'), not 'trivialement'.
(285): the target should read Scind(M̃̃ comme ext. de Γ̃̃ par M); the struck word before 'ext.' is 'considéré/comme'.

The line after (285) reads roughly: '(par conjugaison avec automorphismes intérieurs). La classe de M-conjugaison, ainsi que des scindages, image de E', i.e. the image of E is a single M-conjugacy class of splittings.
'il faut et il suffit que l'élément u = y − x ∈ M soit dans M^Γ = M^{Γ̃̃}' (double tilde intended).
Last lines: 'E s'identifie exactement à une classe de M-conjugaison de scindages de M̃̃.'
